notes:
DELTA BATCH FOR A RELOCATED CHECK, NOT A RE-ADJUDICATION. aurora-lint 4bbf15d1
("EXP34-C: report the callee's unguarded dereference, not the call site",
Brandon's ruling 2026-09-21: a caller passing a possibly-null pointer into a
callee never violates by itself, because C has no contract semantics) moved
EXP34-C's report site. These 130 keys are the in-scope findings at the new tip
(0.5.2 @ ca327445) that the oracle did not already cover.

BASELINE, MEASURED, NOT INHERITED. The task body's "8,900 findings on 11 corpora
at 2960cd88" does not match the database. Measured against Postgres at realworld
run 270 (sqc-0.5.2-2960cd88): EXP34-C raw 10,564 across 12 corpora, 10,426 of
them in scope. Splitting by message shape, the caller-side set 1418 relocates
away is 8,191 (8,187 excluding 4 function-pointer rows), not 8,900, and it spans
all 12 corpora, not 11. Two other quantities are genuinely 11: libcrc is the only
project with zero callee-side findings, and EXP34-C's oracle covers 11 projects
because valkey has never been adjudicated (bmdb 1249). At the new tip the rule
produces 3,325 findings, corroborating dev-921's independent 3,326 within one.

SCOPE OF THIS BATCH. Key-level, run 270 -> ca327445: 10,004 distinct keys ->
3,261; 2,983 survived, 7,021 vanished, 278 are new. In-scope and unlabelled
against Postgres ground_truth is 1,111 rows, of which 980 are valkey -- not this
relocation's doing, but the pre-existing absence of any valkey EXP34-C oracle.
Per the coordinator's 2026-09-22 call those stay with bmdb 1249 as its own
whole-file pass, and this batch is the remaining 131 rows / 130 distinct keys.
The two findings at hostap src/utils/wpabuf.c:40 differ in message but share a
key, and the oracle cannot distinguish them; one row covers both and its reason
addresses each.

METHOD. The unlabelled set was computed by joining the local run against
ground_truth in Postgres, NOT with `bench realworld-unlabeled`: that command
reads this checkout's local SQLite oracle, which is empty on a worker node, so
it would report every finding as unlabelled. Scope was applied with the pinned
scope_include/scope_exclude from audit_corpus_meta via bench_db.corpus.in_scope,
the oracle's own predicate. Note that realworld_violations.file_path is absolute
while ground_truth and the scope globs are repo-relative; the prefix is stripped
before either is applied. corpus-check was green for all 12 checkouts and their
pins match run 270's codebase_commits, so the two runs are comparable.

STANDARD APPLIED. Calibrated against this dataset's existing EXP34-C rows rather
than an invented bar: an FP records that no null-producing expression reaches the
dereference (the shape already recorded at sqlite src/expr.c:47, "callers never
pass NULL"), and a TP requires a concrete null producer on a path that reaches it
(the shape at sqlite ext/expert/expert.c:65, an unchecked sqlite3_malloc64).
Caller sets were enumerated where the set is closed, and confidence is "high"
only where it was; "medium" records reasoning from an invariant rather than a
closed enumeration.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT USED AS A BASIS. Per ADR-0010 Decision 1, no verdict
rests on which macros a build defines -- notably not sqlite's
`# define sqlite3BtreeEnter(X)` under SQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE (src/btree.h:396).
Per Decision 5, no verdict rests on an assertion in either direction: curl's
DEBUGASSERT, hostap's WPA_ASSERT, mbedtls's documented no-null-parameter policy
and sqlite's assert-only routines are all recorded as neutral where they appear.
Two findings were also found to misstate their own basis: the claim "which does
not check for NULL" is false for sqlite3ErrorMsg, whose %#T and %T handlers test
the pointer at src/printf.c:929 and :937 before dereferencing it, and for
hostap's wpabuf.c:40, where the pointer is consumed by a %p conversion, which
does not dereference it at all.

THE 27 TP ROWS ARE ONE FINDING. All are mosquitto src/loop.c, the vararg remnant
4bbf15d1 deliberately kept alive (check_callsite_null_args survives, scoped to
args at or past variadic_from, because a vararg slot carries no positional index
for the callee's own analysis to seed). `id` takes context->address when
context->id is NULL; context->address is initialised NULL at src/context.c:114,
assigned from mosquitto_strdup, and NULL-checked by mosquitto's own code at
src/context.c:51. Every path that leaves it NULL bails except one:
context__init_sock(..., get_address=false) at src/net.c:204, the
enable_proxy_protocol listener path, which returns MOSQ_ERR_SUCCESS on a client
that has no id yet either. The bridge path is not the one -- it guards its id at
src/bridge.c:74-76. The same switch carries a dedicated MOSQ_ERR_PROXY case, so
proxy-path contexts demonstrably reach it. The value is consumed as a %s
conversion by a variadic callee.

NO PRECISION OR RECALL CLAIM follows from this batch, here or anywhere, per
CLAUDE.md's delta-adjudication rule and bmdb 1423 step 3. The stale caller-line
keys are 1423's half: 6,031 labelled keys no longer fire at ca327445 (5,934 FP,
69 TP -- not the 68 that task states -- 21 uncertain, and 7 FN, which that task
does not mention and which are a different problem, since an FN key that no
longer fires is not stale). Separately, run 270 -> ca327445 spans 49+ commits;
MSC13-C moved +1,329 on its own, so no total delta here is attributable to 1418
alone. Isolating that needs 4bbf15d1^ vs 4bbf15d1, which this node did not run.

Adjudicated on dev-180 under aurora_lint 1418.
